$comment: THE FOUR SEASONS - canonical prompt slot order. Every character prompt MUST be assembled by joining the slots below in the declared order with ', '. Do not reorder, do not omit a slot, do not inline extra clauses. The wiki outfit sheets carry the assembled string; this file is the source of truth for how it was built.

slot_definitions.subject: Age, nationality, social role, height and build. Never omit - a prompt without a subject generates a different person on every run.
slot_definitions.eyes: Shape, eyelid, iris colour, brow. Chapter-invariant.
slot_definitions.top: Upper garment: material, colour, and how it is worn.
slot_definitions.bottom: Lower garment: length, silhouette. For one-piece outfits, describe the skirt portion here.
slot_definitions.legwear_shoes: Hosiery plus footwear. The lace-vs-velcro distinction is load-bearing for characterisation - keep the fastening explicit.
slot_definitions.tone: Seasonal palette, contrast level, skin and lighting. Derived from the character's personal-colour assignment.
slot_definitions.expression: The 6-stage expression fragment. Replaces nothing - it is inserted between eyes and framing. See expression_stages.
slot_definitions.framing: Shot framing for expression sheets. Fixed across all characters so the six panels are comparable.
slot_definitions.identity: Compact identity for expression sheets: age, hair, eyes, brows only. The full subject/hair/eyes slots are too long to co-exist with an expression inside one CLIP chunk.

forbidden: real person names (the face_model frontmatter field is an internal casting note, never a prompt token)
pixel art / 16-bit / retro game style tokens (concept dropped)
chapter-specific breakdown state (put that in a per-scene override, not the base prompt)
stage-1 illustration as the IP-Adapter reference for a stage-2 realistic render (style would follow the reference back to illustration)

negative_prompt: worst quality, low quality, bad anatomy, chibi, oversized head, sketch, pixel art, retro game, text, letters, watermark, signature, blurry

tachibana-hiiragi.stage2_constraint: REQUIRED. Hiiragi is 19. Her understated, non-voluptuous figure is a narrative device, not an attempt to look underage: in-story she lies about being unable to clean herself up in order to get an adult woman to undress her, and that lie only has any surface plausibility if her figure is unexaggerated (no D-cup, no flared hips) - it is the realistic floor for the lie to work at all, not a childlike body. Stage 2 for this character must hold unambiguously adult facial structure and proportions at all times, and any output that does not must be discarded rather than adjusted. Her youthfulness is carried by styling and behaviour (round doll-like eyes, soft rounded build, timid affect), never by making the body or face read as a minor.

pipeline.$comment: Two stages. Illustration is not a rejected style - it is the specification layer where human and model agree on what is decided. Realistic is the deliverable.

stage1_illustration.purpose: Fix and agree the features. Exaggerate the readable signs (sweat beads, circular blush, light leaving the eyes) so both a human and a model can confirm what is settled.
stage1_illustration.tone_suffix: clean anime illustration, flat colours, clear linework
stage1_illustration.published_as: 仕様画像（wikiに「仕様」として掲載）

stage2_realistic.tone_suffix: photorealistic, natural skin texture and pores, soft directional lighting, shallow depth of field
stage2_realistic.structure_from: Stage 1 output, via canny_map or depth_map into ControlNet. This is what carries the agreed expression and pose across the style change.
stage2_realistic.identity_from: A realistic reference of the same character. IP-Adapter inherits style from its reference, so the stage-2 reference must already be realistic - a stage-1 illustration would drag the output back to illustration.

token_budget.note: SD1.5 CLIP encodes in 77-token chunks and later chunks carry much less weight. A prompt that overflows silently loses its tail, so the varying slot must come first and the whole string must fit one chunk. Verified empirically: a 186-token prompt dropped the expression, framing and style entirely.

verified_recipe.$comment: Settled by three runs against ComfyUI on 2026-08-11. Do not reintroduce what is listed under failed.
failed: ip_weight 0.85 with a 186-token prompt: expression, framing and style all fell past the CLIP chunk and were ignored - output was a neutral sad face with no sweat
(clause:1.25) emphasis on a whole expression clause: weights every token in it, produced grotesque eyebrows, and turned 'biting lower lip' into a finger held in the mouth
'biting lower lip' as a token at all - reads as a hand gesture. Use 'lips pressed tight'
verified_recipe.works: plain unweighted prompt under 77 tokens, expression wording kept physical and simple, ip_weight 0.75 so the reference does not override the expression
verified_recipe.ip_adapter_tradeoff: Measured on RealVisXL. ip_weight 0.8 / ip_end 0.9 holds the identity exactly but also transfers the reference's neutral expression, and the prompt cannot override it. Dropping to 0.6 / 0.45 lets the expression through but the face becomes a different person. There is no setting that gives both, which is the empirical reason the two-stage pipeline exists: keep ip_weight high for identity and bring the expression in through ControlNet structure taken from the stage-1 illustration, not through the prompt.

flux.$comment: Flux uses T5 alongside CLIP and does not truncate at 77 tokens, so the canon that had to be dropped for SD1.5/SDXL fits here. Written as prose because T5 reads sentences better than comma-stacked tags. This is the fidelity test set: every clause below is traceable to the character note, and anything the render gets wrong is a measurable miss.
flux.negative_prompt: text, watermark, signature, extra fingers, deformed hands, freckles, heavy makeup, high contrast lighting
